Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 4:

(p-202) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Yusuf

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When Joseph said to his father, "O my father, indeed I have seen eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."﴾

He did not explain here the interpretation (ta'wil) of this vision, but he explained it in this noble surah in His saying: ﴿So when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, if Allah wills, in security."﴾ ﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before. My Lord has made it true."﴾ up to the end of the verse [Yusuf: 99, 100].

And it is known that the visions of the prophets are revelation (wahy).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 6:

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿And thus your Lord will choose you and teach you the interpretation of narrations﴾.

Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has made clear that He taught His prophet Yusuf (the interpretation of narrations), and He stated this also in His saying: ﴿And thus We established Yusuf in the land, and that We might teach him the interpretation of narrations﴾ [Yusuf: 21].

And in His saying: ﴿My Lord, You have given me [some] of the kingdom and taught me [some] of the interpretation of narrations﴾ [Yusuf: 101].

The scholars differed concerning what is meant by "the interpretation of narrations" (ta'wil al-ahadith; ta'wil meaning the explanation or ultimate meaning of a thing).

A group of the people of knowledge held that what is meant by this is the interpreting of dreams (ta'bir al-ru'ya), so "narrations" according to this view are dreams. They said: because a dream is either a notion of the soul (hadith nafs), or from an angel, or from a devil.

Yusuf was the most skilled of people in interpreting dreams, and what indicates this aspect are the verses that show his expertise in the interpretation of dreams, such as His saying: ﴿O two companions of the prison, as for one of you, he will give drink to his lord of wine; but as for the other, he will be crucified and birds will eat from his head. The matter has been decided about which you both inquire﴾ [Yusuf: 41], and His saying:

﴿He said, "You will plant for seven years in succession; so what you harvest leave in its ears, except a little of what you eat"﴾ [Yusuf: 47], up to His saying: ﴿...in which they will be given rain and in which they will press [juice]﴾ [Yusuf: 49].

Some scholars said: what is meant by the interpretation of narrations is knowing the meanings of the books of Allah and the sunnahs (ways) of the prophets, and what is obscure and unclear to people of their purposes and objectives; he explains them for them, clarifies them, and guides them to the hidden wisdoms within them.

They were called "narrations" (ahadith) because they are related (yuhaddath) from Allah and His messengers, so it is said: Allah said such-and-such, and His Messenger said such-and-such. Do you not see His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then in what narration after this will they believe?﴾ [Al-A'raf: 185].

And His saying: (p-203) ﴿Allah has sent down the best narration﴾ the verse [Az-Zumar: 23]. What indicates this aspect is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when he reached his maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge﴾ [Al-Qasas: 14], and His saying: ﴿He said, "No food will come to you that you are given but that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me"﴾ the verse [Yusuf: 37].

The one who restricted it (muqayyiduhu), may Allah pardon him, said: The apparent meaning is that the mentioned verses include all of that: the interpretation of dreams, and the sciences of the books of Allah and the sunnahs of the prophets. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When they said: Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, though we are a group. Indeed our father is in clear error.﴾

The apparent meaning is that the intended sense, by the sons of Ya'qub (upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace) in this noble verse, of this error with which they described their father, is only going astray from knowledge of the reality of the matter as it should be known.

What supports this is the occurrence of "error" (ḍalāl) in this sense in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. From its use in this sense is His saying, exalted is He, quoting them addressing their father: ﴿They said: By God, you are surely in your old error﴾ [Yusuf: 95]. And His saying, exalted is He, concerning our Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And He found you lost and guided you﴾ [al-Duha: 7], meaning: you did not have knowledge of these sciences which are not known except through revelation, so He guided you to them and taught you them by what He revealed to you of this great Qur'an. From its use in this sense is also the saying of the poet:

"And Salma thinks that I seek in her a replacement, while I see her bewildered in error."

He means that she, in her assumption that he seeks a replacement for her, is not knowing of the reality, and he does not seek a replacement for her.

The intention of the sons of Ya'qub was not error in the religion; for had they intended that, they would have been disbelievers. Rather, their intention was that their father, in their opinion, was in a departure from perceiving the reality and from placing the matter in its proper station, in that he preferred two over ten, although the ten were more beneficial to him and more capable of carrying out his affairs and managing his matters.

Know that ḍalāl (error, going astray) is used in the Qur'an in two other senses:

The first is error in the religion (ḍalāl fi'l-dīn), i.e., departing from the path of truth which the messengers, may God's prayers and peace be upon them, brought. This is the most well-known of its meanings in the Qur'an, and from its use in this sense is: ﴿not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray﴾ [al-Fatiha: 7], and His saying: ﴿And most of the earlier peoples had already gone astray before them﴾ [al-Saffat: 71], and His saying: ﴿And he had certainly led astray a great multitude from among you﴾ [Ya-Sin: 62], and other verses.

The second is the use of ḍalāl in the sense of perishing and disappearing (al-halāk wa'l-ghaybah), from the saying of the Arabs: "ḍalla al-samnu fi'l-ṭa'ām" (the ghee was lost/dissolved in the food), when it became hidden in it and perished in it. For this reason the Arabs call burial iḍlāl (causing to go astray), because it is a concealment in the earth which results in the consumption of the bones of the dead therein, for they become dust and mix with the earth. From its use in this sense is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: When we have gone astray in the earth...﴾ the verse [al-Sajdah: 10].

From the use of ḍalāl to mean absence is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what they used to invent has vanished from them﴾ [al-A'raf: 53], meaning: it disappeared and was obliterated.

From the use of ḍalāl to mean burial is the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

"So those who buried him returned with a clear report, and Hazm and Na'il were left behind at al-Jawlan."

So his saying "muḍilluhu" means those who buried him; his saying "bi-'ayn jaliyyah" means with a certain report; and al-Jawlan is a mountain near which the aforementioned was buried.

From ḍalāl in the sense of absence and obliteration is the saying of al-Akhtal:

"I was a speck in a turbid, foaming wave, which the torrent cast forth, and it went completely astray."

And the saying of another:

"Did you not ask, so that the abodes might inform you, about the tribe that was lost, where they went?"

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they took him away and agreed to put him in the depths of the well, We revealed to him: "You will surely inform them of this matter of theirs, while they do not perceive."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted informs us that He revealed to Yusuf, upon him and upon our Prophet be blessings and peace, that he would inform his brothers of this matter which they had done to him, while they were not aware.

Then, in this noble surah, He explicitly stated that He, exalted and majestic, fulfilled that promise in His saying: ﴿He said, "Do you know what you did with Yusuf and his brother when you were ignorant?"﴾ [Yusuf: 89].

And He explicitly stated their lack of awareness that he was Yusuf in His saying: ﴿The brothers of Yusuf came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him.﴾ [Yusuf: 58].

What we have mentioned, that the governing element of the circumstantial clause (al-jumla al-haliyya) is His saying "la-tunabbi'annahum" [Yusuf: 15], meaning: "you will surely inform them of this matter of theirs while they do not perceive that you are Yusuf," is the apparent meaning.

It was also said that the governing element of the circumstantial clause is His saying "wa-awhayna ilayhi" [Yusuf: 15], and according to this the meaning is that this revelation occurred while they did not perceive that it was being revealed to him.

The majority of reciters read this verse: "ghayabati al-jubb" [Yusuf: 15] in the singular. Nafi' read "ghayabat al-jubb" in the plural form. Everything that conceals something from you is a ghayaba (depths/hidden place), and from this it was said that the grave is called a ghayaba. From this is the saying of the poet:

"And if one day my hidden depth conceals me, then travel in my manner among the tribe and the family."

The plural in Nafi's reading is in view of the multiplicity of parts of the bottom of the well which hide whoever enters it from sight.

The scholars differed regarding the answer (jawab) of "lamma" in His saying ﴿So when they took him away﴾: is it expressed or omitted?

It was said: it is expressed, and it is His saying: ﴿They said, "O our father, we went racing"﴾ and so on [Yusuf: 17], i.e., "when such and such was the case, they said, 'O our father'." Abu Hayyan preferred this view.

It was also said: the answer of "lamma" is His saying "awhayna" [Yusuf: 15], and the waw is extra (silah). This is the position of the Kufans, who hold that the waw is added to the answer of "lamma," "hatta," and "idha." On this basis they explained His saying: ﴿So when they both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead, and We called out to him﴾ and so on [al-Saffat: 103-104], and His saying: ﴿Until, when they came to it and its gates were opened﴾ and so on [al-Zumar: 73], and the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"So when we crossed the courtyard of the tribe and it veered with us toward the belly of a sand dune rich in debris and winding."

That is: when we crossed the courtyard of the tribe, it veered.

It was also said: the answer of "lamma" is omitted, and this is the view of the Basrans. Its estimated form was disputed. It was said that its estimate is: "they did to him what they did of harm."

Some estimated it: "So when they took him away and agreed to put him in the depths of the well, their trial became great."

Some estimated it: "So when they took him away and agreed to put him in the depths of the well, they placed him in it."

Abu Hayyan favored this last view, because His saying: ﴿and agreed to put him﴾ [Yusuf: 15] indicates this estimated element. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 24 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed she desired him, and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Lord.﴾

The apparent meaning of this noble verse may give the impression that Yusuf, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace, intended to do with that woman the same as she intended with him. However, the Noble Qur'an clarified his innocence from falling into what is not befitting, by mentioning the testimony of everyone who has a connection to the matter to his innocence, as well as God's testimony to that and the acknowledgment of Iblis of it.

As for those who have a connection to that incident, they are: Yusuf, the woman, her husband, the women, (p-206) and the witnesses.

As for Yusuf's certainty that he was innocent of that sin, God mentioned it in His saying: ﴿She sought to seduce me from myself﴾ [Yusuf: 26], and His saying: ﴿He said: "My Lord, the prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me."﴾

As for the woman's acknowledgment of this, it is in her saying to the women: ﴿And I did seek to seduce him from himself, but he refrained.﴾ [Yusuf: 32], and her saying: ﴿Now the truth has become manifest. It was I who sought to seduce him from himself, and indeed he is of the truthful.﴾ [Yusuf: 51].

As for the acknowledgment of the woman's husband, it is in His saying: ﴿He said: "Indeed, it is of your plotting. Indeed, your plotting is great."﴾ ﴿"Yusuf, turn away from this, and ask forgiveness for your sin, for indeed you were of the wrongdoers."﴾ [Yusuf: 28, 29].

As for the acknowledgment of the witnesses to this, it is in His saying: ﴿And a witness from her family testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is of the liars."﴾ and the verse [Yusuf: 26].

As for God's testimony of his innocence, azza wa jall, it is in His saying: ﴿Thus, that We might avert from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.﴾ [Yusuf: 24].

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said in his Tafsir: Allah, exalted is He, has testified in this noble verse to his purity four times:

The first: ﴿That We might avert from him evil﴾, where the lam is for emphasis and intensification.

The second: His saying "and immorality", i.e., thus that We might avert from him immorality.

The third: His saying ﴿Indeed, he was of Our servants﴾, although He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ [Al-Furqan: 63].

The fourth: His saying "the chosen (al-mukhlasin)", and in it there are two readings: one with the active participle, and another with the passive participle.

Its occurrence with the active participle indicates his being one who performs acts of obedience and devotions along with the attribute of sincerity.

Its occurrence with the passive participle indicates that Allah, exalted is He, chose him for Himself and selected him for His presence.

On both readings, it is among the clearest expressions indicating his being exempt from what they attributed to him. End quote from the Tafsir of al-Razi.

This is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "God forbid! Indeed, he is my lord; he has made my residence good. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."﴾ [Yusuf: 23].

(p-207) As for Iblis's acknowledgment of Yusuf's purity and freedom from blame, it is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them."﴾ [Sad: 82, 83]. So he acknowledged that he is unable to mislead the chosen ones, and there is no doubt that Yusuf is among the chosen ones, as God explicitly stated in His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.﴾ Thus the indication of the Qur'an became manifest from multiple aspects regarding his innocence from what is not befitting.

Al-Razi also said in his commentary on this verse, in its wording: And at this point we say: those ignorant people who attributed this disgrace to Yusuf, peace be upon him, if they are followers of the religion of Allah, exalted is He, then let them accept the testimony of Allah, exalted is He, to his purity; and if they are followers of Iblis and his soldiers, then let them accept the testimony of Iblis to his purity. Perhaps they would say: "We were at first students of Iblis, until we graduated under him, and then we increased in foolishness beyond him," as al-Khwarazmi said:

"I was a man among the soldiers of Iblis, until time elevated me until Iblis became one of my soldiers.
If he had died before me, I would have excelled after him in the ways of wickedness, which none excels in after me."

Thus by these proofs it is established that Yusuf, peace be upon him, is innocent of what these ignorant people say. End of al-Razi's words.

There is no hiding the lack of adab in this toward those who said that statement from among the Companions and the scholars of the righteous predecessors. The excuse of al-Razi in this is his belief that this was not established from any of the righteous predecessors.

You will see at the end of this discussion the statements of the scholars on this question, God willing, exalted is He.

If it is said: You have explained the Qur'an's indication of his innocence, peace be upon him, from what is not befitting in the preceding verses, but what do you say about His saying: ﴿And he would have desired her﴾? [Yusuf: 24]

The answer is in two respects:

The first: What is meant by Yusuf's desire for her is a heart-thought that was turned away from him by the restraint of piety. Some have said: it is the natural inclination and the innate desire restrained by piety, and there is no sin in this, because it is a matter of disposition that is not subject to legal obligation, as in the hadith: "He, ﷺ, used to divide between his wives, being just, then he would say: 'O Allah, this is my division in what I own, so do not blame me for what I do not own,'" meaning the natural inclination of the heart.

An example of this is the fasting person's natural inclination toward cold water, although his piety prevents him from drinking while he is fasting. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, a complete good deed is recorded for him," because he left what his soul naturally inclines to, out of fear of Allah and in compliance with His command, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But as for one who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from [its] desire, Indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 40, 41].

The intention of the Banu Harithah and the Banu Salamah to flee on the day of Uhud was like this intention of Yusuf, as is evident from His saying: ﴿When two parties among you were about to lose heart, but Allah was their ally.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 122], because His saying "but Allah was their ally" indicates that this intention was not a sin; for following a sin with Allah's guardianship of the sinner would be an incitement to sin.

The Arabs use the term "hamm" and mean by it love and desire. A person says of what he does not love or desire: "This does not concern me (ma yuhimmuni)," and says of what he loves and desires: "This is the most important thing to me (ahamm al-ashya' ilayya)." This is unlike the desire of the wife of al-Aziz, which was a desire of resolve and determination, as is evident from the fact that she tore his shirt from behind while he was fleeing from her, and nothing prevented her from falling into what is not befitting except her own inability to do so.

Such determination upon sin is itself a sin for which its doer is held accountable, as is evident from the authentic hadith in the Sahih from him, ﷺ, from the hadith of Abu Bakrah: "When two Muslims meet with their swords, the killer and the killed are in the Fire." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we understand the killer, but what about the killed?" He said: "Indeed, he was eager to kill his companion." So he, ﷺ, explicitly stated that the resolve to kill his companion is a sin for which Allah caused him to enter the Fire.

As for their interpretation of Yusuf's desire as meaning that he approached desire but did not actually desire in deed, like the saying of the Arabs: "I would have killed him, had I not feared Allah," meaning I came close to killing him, as al-Zamakhshari said.

And interpreting the desire as meaning that he intended to strike her, or intended to push her away from himself, all of that is not apparent; rather it is far from the apparent meaning and has no evidence.

The second answer, which is the choice of Abu Hayyan: that no desire at all arose in Yusuf; rather it is negated from him because of the existence of the proof.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: This view which Abu Hayyan and others chose is the most consistent of the opinions with the rules of the Arabic language, because the common practice in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs is that the omitted answer is preceded by something that indicates it, as in His saying: ﴿And upon Him rely, if you are believers.﴾ [Yunus: 84], meaning: if you are believers, then rely upon Him. The first part is the indicator of the omitted answer, not the answer itself, because the answer of conditionals and the answer of "law lawla" does not precede; rather what is mentioned before it serves as an indicator of it, like the verse mentioned, and like His saying: ﴿Say, "Produce your proof, if you are truthful."﴾ [An-Naml: 64], meaning: if you are truthful, then produce your proof.

According to this view, the meaning of the verse "And he would have desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord" is: had he not seen it, he would have desired her. So what precedes "law lawla" is the indicator of the omitted answer, as is the common practice in the Qur'an and the language.

A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And she was about to reveal him, had We not bound fast her heart so that she would be among the believers.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 10], so what precedes "law lawla" is the indicator of the answer, meaning: had We not bound fast her heart, she would have revealed him.

Know that a group of scholars of Arabic permitted the anteposition of the answer of "law lawla" [Yusuf: 24], and the anteposition of the answer in all other conditionals. According to this view, the answer of "law lawla" in His saying: ﴿Had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ [Yusuf: 24] is what precedes it in His saying: ﴿And he would have desired her﴾ [Yusuf: 24].

To this permissibility of the mentioned anteposition went the Kufans, and among the leading Basrans: Abu al-Abbas al-Mubarrad, and Abu Zayd al-Ansari.

Shaykh Abu Hayyan said in "al-Bahr al-Muhit," in its wording: What I choose is that Yusuf, peace be upon him, never had any desire for her at all; rather it is negated because of the seeing of the proof, as you say: "You would have committed it, had Allah not protected you." We do not say that the answer of "law lawla" precedes it, although no evidence establishes the impossibility of that. Indeed, the explicit conditional particles that govern are disputed regarding the permissibility of anteposing their answers, and this was the view of the Kufans, and among the leading Basrans: Abu Zayd al-Ansari and Abu al-Abbas al-Mubarrad.

Rather, we say: the answer of "law lawla" is omitted, because what precedes it indicates it, as the Basran majority says regarding the Arab saying: "You are a wrongdoer if you do it." They estimate it as: "If you do it, then you are a wrongdoer," and his saying "you are a wrongdoer" does not indicate the establishment of wrongdoing; rather it is affirmed on the assumption of the existence of the act. Likewise here the estimate is: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have desired her," so the existence of the desire was conditional on the non-seeing of the proof, but he saw the proof and so the desire was negated. We pay no attention to the view of al-Zajjaj. Had the statement been "and he would have desired her" (with the lam), it would have been far-fetched; how much more so with the lam dropped? Because it gives the false impression that His saying "and he desired her" is the answer of "law lawla," and we did not say that. Rather it is the indicator of the answer. Even if it were the answer itself, the lam is not obligatory, since the answer of "law lawla" when in the past tense may come with the lam or without it. You say: "Had it not been for Zayd, I would have honored you," and "Had it not been for Zayd, I honored you." So whoever holds that His saying "he desired her" is the answer itself is not far off. And no attention is paid to the saying of Ibn Atiyyah: that the statement of those who say that the speech is complete at His saying "And she indeed desired him," and that the answer of "law lawla" is in His saying "and he desired her," and that the meaning is: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have desired her," so Yusuf, peace be upon him, did not desire. He said: This is a view which the tongue of the Arabs and the sayings of the predecessors refute. End quote.

As for his saying that "the tongue of the Arabs refutes it," it is not as he stated. Those who held the permissibility of this have argued by its existence in the tongue of the Arabs. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿She was about to reveal him, had We not bound fast her heart so that she would be among the believers.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 10]. So His saying "she was about to reveal him" can either be explained according to what that speaker held, or it can be explained according to what we have held, that it is the indicator of the answer, and the estimate is: "Had We not bound fast her heart, she would have revealed him."

As for the sayings of the predecessors: we believe that nothing of that is authentically transmitted from any of them, because they are mutually contradictory statements, some of which refute others, besides being damaging even for some sinful Muslims, let alone those who are attested to be protected from sin.

What is transmitted from the predecessors is not supported by the speech of the Arabs, because they estimated the answer of "law lawla" as omitted with no evidence indicating it, since they did not estimate "desire for her," and the speech of the Arabs only indicates that the omitted element is from the meaning of what precedes the condition, because what precedes the condition is the indicator of it. End of the point of relevance from Abu Hayyan's words in his own wording.

And indeed we have already mentioned that this view is the most consistent of the opinions with the language of the Arabs, even though some scholars claim otherwise.

By these two answers you know that Yusuf, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, is free from falling into what is not befitting. Either he never committed anything of the sort at all, on the basis that the "hamm" (intention) is linked to the particle of prohibition, which is "law" (had it not been), meaning the absence of seeing the proof; and he did see the proof, so what was conditioned upon it is negated, and with its negation the conditioned matter, which is his intention toward her, is negated, as was previously clarified in the words of Abu Hayyan.

Or else his intention was a fleeting inner thought which was turned away from him by the restraint of piety, or it was the desire and natural inclination restrained by piety, as we have explained. With this it becomes clear to you that His saying: ﴿And he certainly intended her﴾ does not contradict what we have presented of the verses proving Yusuf's freedom from falling into what is not befitting.

Now that you know, from what we have explained, the indication of the Great Qur'an to his freedom from what is not befitting, we will mention to you the views of the scholars who said that he did commit some of what is not befitting, and their views on what is meant by "the proof." So we say:

The author of "ad-Durr al-Manthur fi at-Tafsir bil-Ma'thur" said: 'Abd ar-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu ash-Shaykh, and al-Hakim (who authenticated it) narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he said: When she intended him, she adorned herself, then lay down on her bed, and he intended her, sat between her legs, and began to untie his trousers. He was called from the sky: "O son of Ya'qub, do not be like a bird whose feathers are plucked, so that it remains without feathers." He did not heed the call at all, until he saw the proof of his Lord: Jibril, peace be upon him, in the form of Ya'qub, biting on his fingers. He was frightened, and his desire came out from his fingertips. He leapt to the door and found it locked, so Yusuf raised his leg and struck the lower door with it, and it opened for him. She followed him and caught up with him, and she put her hands on his shirt and tore it until it reached the muscle of his calf. They found their master at the door.

Ibn Jarir, Abu ash-Shaykh, and Abu Nu'aym in "al-Hilyah" narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he was asked about how far Yusuf's intention, peace be upon him, went. He said: He untied the hempyan (i.e., the trousers) and sat in her position like one who circumcises, then he was called out to: "O Yusuf, do not be like the bird that has feathers; when it commits fornication it sits without feathers!"

Abu Nu'aym in "al-Hilyah" narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: ﴿And she certainly intended him, and he would have intended her﴾ [Yusuf: 24], that he said: She desired him and he desired her, and from the desire he intended to untie the belt. She got up to an idol adorned with pearls and rubies in a corner of the house, and covered it with a white garment between her and it. He said: "What are you doing?" She said: "I am shy before my God that He should see me in this state." Yusuf, peace be upon him, said: "You are shy before an idol that neither eats nor drinks, and I am not shy before my God who is watching over every soul for what it has earned?" Then he said: "You shall never get it from me." And this is the proof he saw.

'Abd ar-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu ash-Shaykh narrated from Mujahid, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: "And he intended her" [Yusuf: 24], that he said: He untied his trousers until they reached his navel, and sat in her position like a man with his wife. Then Ya'qub, peace be upon him, was depicted to him, and he struck his chest with his hand, and his desire came out from his fingertips.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu ash-Shaykh, and al-Hakim (who authenticated it) narrated from Ibn 'Abbas (p-212), may Allah be pleased with him and his father, regarding His saying: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord," he said: He saw the image of his father Ya'qub in the middle of the house, biting on his thumb, so he turned away fleeing and said: "By your right, O father, I shall never return again."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu ash-Shaykh narrated from 'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His saying: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord," they both said: He untied the trousers and sat in her position like one who circumcises, then he saw an image in which was the face of Ya'qub biting on his fingers, so he pushed his chest and the desire came out from his fingertips. Every son of Ya'qub was born to him twelve sons except Yusuf, peace be upon him, for he was deprived of a son by that desire, so he had only eleven sons.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Mujahid, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord," he said: Ya'qub, peace be upon him, was depicted to him, and he struck Yusuf's chest, and his desire flew out from the tips of his fingers. So every son of Ya'qub was born with twelve males, except Yusuf, to whom only two sons were born.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu ash-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord," he said: He saw Ya'qub biting on his fingers, saying: "Yusuf! Yusuf!"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu ash-Shaykh narrated from Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding the verse, he said: He saw one of the signs of his Lord by which Allah restrained him from His disobedience. It was mentioned to us that Ya'qub was depicted to him biting on his two fingers, and he was saying to him: "O Yusuf! Will you intend the deeds of fools, while you are written among the prophets?!" That is the proof. Allah removed every desire that was in his joints.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu ash-Shaykh narrated from Muhammad ibn Sirin, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord," he said: Ya'qub, peace be upon him, was depicted to him biting on his two fingers, saying: "Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, the friend of the Most Merciful, your name is written among the prophets, and you do the deeds of fools!"

'Abd ar-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Mujahid, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: He saw the image of Ya'qub, peace be upon him, in the wall.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu ash-Shaykh narrated from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: They claim that the ceiling of the house opened, and he saw Ya'qub biting on his two fingers.

(p-213) 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated in "Zawa'id az-Zuhd" from al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: "And she certainly intended him, and he would have intended her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord." He said: When he intended, it was said to him: "Raise your head, O Yusuf." He raised his head, and behold, there was an image on the ceiling of the house saying: "O Yusuf! O Yusuf! You are written among the prophets!" So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, protected him.

Abu 'Ubayd, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abu Salih, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: He saw the image of Ya'qub on the ceiling of the house saying: "Yusuf! Yusuf!"

Ibn Jarir narrated through the route of az-Zuhri that Humayd ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman informed him that the proof which Yusuf, peace be upon him, saw was Ya'qub.

Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah: It was called out: "O son of Ya'qub, do not be like the bird that has feathers; when it commits fornication it sits without feathers." He did not heed the call and sat, then he raised his head and saw the face of Ya'qub biting on his finger, so he stood up trembling, out of shame before his father.

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, who said: Every man among them had twelve sons born to him, except that Yusuf, peace be upon him, had eleven born to him, because of what came out of his desire.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Shimr ibn 'Atiyyah, who said: Yusuf looked at the image of Ya'qub biting on his finger, saying: "O Yusuf!" At that moment he refrained and stood up.

Ibn Jarir narrated from ad-Dahhak, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: They claim that Ya'qub, peace be upon him, was depicted to him, and he was shy before him.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Awza'i, who said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, used to say regarding His saying: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord," he said: He saw a verse from the Book of Allah, and it restrained him; it was depicted to him on the wall of the house.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The proof which Yusuf, peace be upon him, saw was three verses from the Book of Allah: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording; they know what you do﴾ [Al-Infitar: 10-12], and the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And you are not in any matter, nor recite of it any Qur'an, nor do any deed, except that We are witness over you when you are involved therein﴾ [Yunus: 61], and the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who associate partners with Him]?﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 33].

(p-214) Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu ash-Shaykh narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: He saw written on the wall in a corner of the house: ﴿And do not approach fornication. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and evil way﴾ [Al-Isra: 32]. Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu ash-Shaykh narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When Yusuf and the wife of the chieftain were alone, a hand without a body came out between them, on which was written in Hebrew: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned?﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 33]. Then the hand withdrew, and they returned to their places. Then the hand came back with writing on it in Hebrew: ﴿Indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording; they know what you do﴾ [Al-Infitar: 10-12]. Then the hand withdrew, and they returned to their places. Then the third hand returned with writing on it: ﴿And do not approach fornication. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and evil way﴾ [Al-Isra: 32]. The hand withdrew, and they returned to their places. Then the fourth hand returned with writing on it in Hebrew: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 281]. Then Yusuf, peace be upon him, fled.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, regarding His saying: "Had he not seen the proof of his Lord," he said: "The signs of his Lord": he was shown the statue of the king.

Abu ash-Shaykh and Abu Nu'aym in "al-Hilyah" narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When Yusuf entered the house with her, and in the house there was a golden idol, she said: "Wait, until I cover the idol, for I am shy before it." Yusuf said: "She is shy before an idol, and I am more deserving to be shy before Allah?" So he refrained from her and left her. End of quotation from "ad-Durr al-Manthur fi at-Tafsir bil-Ma'thur."

The compiler of this work, may Allah forgive him, says: These reports which you have seen attributed to these scholars are divided into two parts:

One part whose transmission is not established from the one who narrated it from them by a sound chain, and there is no problem in discarding this.

And a part which is established from some of those mentioned, and whoever is established as having reported something of it, then the apparent and dominant view that is close to certainty is that he received it from the Isra'iliyyat, since there is no room for opinion in it, and nothing of it, little or much, was raised to the Prophet ﷺ.

By this you know that it is not befitting to be bold in saying about the Prophet of Allah Yusuf that he sat between the legs of a foreign disbelieving woman, intending to commit fornication with her, relying on such narrations, especially since in the narrations (p-215) mentioned there are signs of fabrication, such as the story of the hand that came out to him four times, and in three of them he did not care about it; for that, even if it were authentic, would be the greatest deterrent for common sinners, so what do you think about the best of the prophets? Moreover, we have already presented the Qur'an's indication of his innocence from several aspects, and we have clarified that the reality does not go beyond one of two matters:

Either no intention toward her occurred from him at all, based on his intention being linked to the absence of seeing the proof, and he did see the proof; or his intention was the natural inclination restrained by piety, and knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of the evil and the immorality, which Allah mentioned in this verse that He turned away from His prophet Yusuf.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His words ﴿That We may turn away from him evil and immorality﴾ [Yusuf: 24], that he said: "Fornication, and bad speech." End of quote.

Some scholars said: "The evil (al-suʾ) is the preliminaries of immorality, such as kissing, and the immorality (al-fahsha") is fornication."

It was also said: "The evil is the transgression of the hand, and the immorality is fornication." The most apparent of the opinions concerning what the kaf in His words ﴿Thus﴾ relates to is that it means: "We did that for him by showing him the proof (al-burhan)." So the thing that is like this is the act, ﴿that We may turn away﴾, and the lam is the lam of purpose (lam kay).

As for His words ﴿the sincere servants﴾ [Yusuf: 24]: Nafiʿ, ʿAsim, Hamzah and al-Kisai read it with a fatha on the lam, in the form of the passive participle (ism al-maful). Ibn ʿAmir, Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read it with a kasra on the lam, in the form of the active participle (ism al-fail). And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted. End of quote.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And a witness from her family testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is of the liars. But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is of the truthful."﴾ ﴿So when he saw that his shirt was torn from the back, he said: "Indeed, it is of your guile (kaydikunna); surely your guile is great."﴾

It is understood from this verse that it is obligatory to judge by a clear circumstantial evidence (qarina) that indicates the truthfulness of one of the two litigants and the falsehood of the other. This is because Allah's mention of this story, in the context of accepting the inference from that circumstance as proof of Joseph's innocence, indicates that judging by the like of that is correct and right. The shirt being torn from its back is a clear proof that he was fleeing from her while she was clutching at him from behind. But He, exalted is He, has explained in another place that the place of acting upon circumstantial evidence is so long as it is not opposed by a circumstance stronger than it (p-216). If a stronger circumstance opposes it, it nullifies it. This is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they came upon his shirt with false blood. He said: "Rather, your souls have beautified for you a matter, so patience is fitting."﴾ [Yusuf: 18]. This is because when the sons of Ya'qub put Yusuf into the bottom of the well, they put on his shirt the blood of a young goat, so that the presence of blood on his shirt would be evidence for the truthfulness of their claim that the wolf had eaten him. There is no doubt that blood is evidence of the wolf's having mauled him, but Ya'qub nullified this evidence of theirs with a stronger evidence, namely the shirt not being torn. So he said: "Glory be to Allah! When has a wolf been gentle and clever, killing Yusuf and not tearing his shirt?" For this reason he openly denied their claim in His saying: ﴿Rather, your souls have beautified for you a matter, so patience is fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe.﴾ [Yusuf: 18].

These mentioned verses are a foundation for judging by circumstantial evidence.

Among the examples of judging by circumstantial evidence: a man marries a woman without having seen her beforehand, and maidservants escort her to him. Their testimony does not establish that this is the particular woman with whom the contract was made, so it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her without needing a proof that witnesses her identity as the one to whom the contract was made, relying upon the circumstance of marriage.

Likewise, a man who lodges as a guest with a people, and a maidservant or a boy brings him food. It is permissible for him to eat without needing anything that proves the owner of the food's permission for him to eat, relying upon the circumstance.

Likewise the saying of Malik and those who agree with him: whoever has the smell of wine detected on his mouth is subject to the prescribed punishment for drinking, relying upon the circumstance, because the presence of its smell on his mouth is evidence that he drank it. Likewise the cases of al-lawth (presumptive evidence) and other matters.

We have already mentioned, in surah al-Ma'ida, the validity of relying on such circumstances, and we explained with the Qur'anic proofs, most clearly, that the verified position is that the law of those before us which is established in our law is law for us, unless there is a proof of abrogation (naskh), and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of His saying: ﴿And they came upon his shirt with false blood﴾ [Yusuf: 18]:

The jurists have used this verse as evidence for acting upon indicators (amarat) in some matters of jurisprudence, such as the qasama (oath procedure in homicide cases) and others, and they have agreed that Ya'qub, peace be upon him, used the soundness of the shirt as evidence against their lie.

Thus it is incumbent upon the examiner to take note of indicators and signs when they conflict; whichever of them is preponderant, he decides in favour of the side of preponderance, which is the strength of the accusation. There is no disagreement about judging by it, as said by Ibn al-'Arabi. End of al-Qurtubi's words.

(p-217) The scholars differed concerning the witness in His saying: ﴿And a witness from her family testified﴾ [Yusuf: 26].

Some scholars said: he was an infant in the cradle. Among those who said so were Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he was a man with a beard, and similarly from al-Hasan.

It is reported from Zayd ibn Aslam that he was a paternal cousin of hers who was wise, and similarly from Qatada and 'Ikrima.

It is reported from Mujahid that he was neither a human nor a jinn; he was a creature of Allah's creation.

The compiler of this work, may Allah pardon him, says: Mujahid's view is refuted by His saying: "from her family" [Yusuf: 26], for it is explicit that he was a human from the woman's family. The most apparent of the views is that he was an infant, because of what Ahmad, Ibn Jarir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Four spoke while they were infants: the son of Pharaoh's hairdresser, the witness of Yusuf, the companion of Jurayj, and 'Isa son of Maryam." End.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 28:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your plotting is tremendous.﴾

When this noble verse is combined with another verse, it becomes clear that the plotting of women is greater than the plotting of Satan. The other verse referred to is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the plotting of Satan is ever weak.﴾ [al-Nisa': 76]. This is because His saying about women, ﴿Indeed, your plotting is tremendous﴾ [Yusuf: 28], and His saying about Satan, ﴿Indeed, the plotting of Satan is ever weak﴾ [al-Nisa': 76], indicate that their plotting is greater than his.

Al-Qurtubi said: Muqatil narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the plotting of women is greater than the plotting of Satan," because Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the plotting of Satan is ever weak﴾, and He says: ﴿Indeed, your plotting is tremendous.﴾ End of quotation.

And the man of letters al-Hasan ibn Ayah al-Hasani al-Shinqiti said:

"The Lord did not regard their plotting as great, except that they are what they are."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 31:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they said, "Far be Allah from imperfection! This is not a human. This is none but a noble angel."﴾ ﴿She said, "That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I certainly sought to seduce him, but he refused."﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted makes clear the praise these women gave Yusuf for these commendable qualities among themselves. Then He makes clear their acknowledgment of that when the king questioned them before the people, in His words: ﴿The king said, "What was your db when you sought to seduce Yusuf?" They said, "Far be Allah from imperfection! We know of him no evil." The wife of the chief said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful."﴾ [Yusuf: 51] and so on.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 100:**

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-309) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Yusuf

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He brought you from the desert﴾ — the verse.

The apparent meaning of this verse indicates that some of the prophets may have been sent from the desert (al-badiyah). Elsewhere, however, there is something that indicates the opposite, namely His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109].

Answers have been given to this in several ways. Among them: Ya'qub (Jacob) was given prophethood while in al-Hadar (settled areas), and then he later moved to the desert (al-badiyah).

Among them also: the intended meaning of "al-badw" is the dwelling at a place named Bada, which is the one mentioned in the verse of Jamil or Kuthayyir:

"You are the one who made Shaghab beloved to me, over Bada; and my homelands are other lands besides these two.
I dwelt in this once, and then once again, so both valleys became pleasant to me."

This view is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and after this view, its weakness is not hidden, as al-Alusi pointed out in his tafsir.

Among them also: the desert from which they came is adjacent to the settled area (al-hadar), so it has the same ruling as it, and Allah knows best.

(p-218) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you were not with them when they resolved on their affair while they were scheming.﴾

Here He does not specify what it was that they resolved upon, nor does He here specify the intended meaning of their scheming. However, at the beginning of this noble surah He did explain that what they resolved upon was placing him at the bottom of the well (ghayabat al-jubb), and that their scheming was what they did to their father Ya'qub (Jacob) and their brother Yusuf (Joseph). This is in His saying: ﴿So when they took him away and agreed to put him into the depths of the well,﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.﴾ [Yusuf: 18].

In this noble verse, He has also indicated the truth of the prophethood of our Prophet ﷺ, because He sent down this Qur'an to him and detailed for him this story, even though he ﷺ was not present with the sons of Ya'qub when they resolved on their scheme against him and on placing him at the bottom of the well. Had Allah not revealed that to him, he would not have known it of his own accord.

There are many verses that point to the proof of his messengership, by way of his informing about past stories whose realities he could not know except through revelation, such as His saying: ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens, [to see] which of them would be entrusted with Maryam﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 44].

And His saying: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Musa the command﴾ [al-Qasas: 44].

And His saying: ﴿And you were not a dweller among the people of Madyan﴾ [al-Qasas: 45].

And His saying: ﴿And you were not on the side of the mount when We called, but it is a mercy from your Lord﴾ [al-Qasas: 46].

And His saying: ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they disputed. It is only revealed to me that I am a clear warner﴾ [Sad: 69, 70].

And His saying: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew it before this﴾ [Hud: 49], along with other verses.

These verses are among the clearest evidences that he ﷺ is a noble messenger, although the striking miracles that indicate this are more than can be counted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 106:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they are associating others with Him.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, 'Amir al-Sha'bi, and most of the exegetes said: The meaning of this verse is that most people, namely the disbelievers, did not believe in Allah in His tawhid (affirmation of His oneness) regarding His lordship (rububiyyah) except that they were associating others with Him in His worship ('ibadah).

Thus, what is meant by their belief is their acknowledgment that He is their Lord, who is their Creator and the Manager of their affairs, and what is meant by their association is their worship of others alongside Him. The verses indicating this meaning are very numerous,

• such as His saying: ﴿Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living? And who arranges [every] matter?" They will say, "Allah." So say, "Then will you not fear Him?"﴾ [Yunus: 31] (p-219),

• and His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they deluded?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87],

• and His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "They were created by the Exalted in Might, the Knowing."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 9],

• and His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they deluded?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 61],

• and His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down rain from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah." But most of them do not reason.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 63],

• and His saying: ﴿Say, "To whom belong the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?" They will say, "To Allah." Say, "Then will you not remember?" Say, "Who is Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the great Throne?" They will say, "[They belong] to Allah." Say, "Then will you not fear Him?" Say, "In whose hand is the dominion of all things, who protects while none can protect against Him, if you should know?" They will say, "[It belongs] to Allah." Say, "Then how are you deluded?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 84–88],

along with other verses besides these.

Yet despite this, they said: ﴿Has he made the gods one God? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing!﴾ [Sad: 5].

These Qur'anic verses indicate that tawhid of lordship does not save from disbelief unless it is accompanied by tawhid of worship, that is, the worship of Allah alone with no partner. This is supported by the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they are associating others with Him﴾ [Yusuf: 106].

There is a difficulty in this noble verse: it is established in the science of rhetoric (balaghah) that the ḥāl (circumstantial clause) is a qualifier of its governing verb and a description of its subject. Accordingly, the governing verb of this circumstantial clause, which is "yu'minu" (believe), is qualified by it, so the meaning becomes the restriction of their belief by their being associators, and this is problematic because of the incompatibility between belief and association.

The one who qualifies it (al-Shinqiti), may Allah pardon him, said: I have not seen anyone who has relieved the difficulty in this matter, and what appears to me, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that this belief qualified by the state of association is only linguistic belief (imān lughawī), not legal belief (imān shar'ī); for whoever worships another alongside Allah is not at all truly called a believer in the legal sense.

As for linguistic belief, it includes every affirmation (taṣdīq). So the disbeliever's affirmation that Allah is the Creator and Provider is called belief linguistically despite his disbelief in Allah, but it is not called belief legally.

When you have verified this, you will know that linguistic belief can coexist with association, so there is no difficulty in qualifying it by that. Likewise is the submission (islām) that exists without belief in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "You have not believed, but say, 'We have submitted,' and faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14]. It is linguistic submission, because legal submission is not found in one in whose heart belief has not entered; and knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

(p-220) Some scholars said: "The verse ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they are associating others with Him﴾ [Yusuf: 106] was revealed concerning the saying of the disbelievers in their talbiyah: 'Here I am, there is no partner for You, except a partner who belongs to You, whom You own and who does not own.'" This also returns to what we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 12, verse 111:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding.﴾

Allah, Mighty and Exalted, mentions in this verse that in the accounts of the messengers with their peoples, and how Allah saved the believers and destroyed the disbelievers, there is a lesson (ʿibrah) for those of understanding (ulu al-albab), that is, an admonition for people of intellect.

He has explained this meaning in many verses, such as His saying concerning the people of Lot: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and by night. Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Saffat: 137], as the indication to it has been mentioned repeatedly before. And knowledge is with Allah, Exalted.
